profile.summary_simple: NASA studied cool flames on the space station. These are low-temperature flames around fuel droplets. Scientists tested different fuels, pressures, and helium mixtures to learn how cool flames burn and go out.
profile.summary_expert: The Cool Flames Investigation (CFI) ran on the ISS from January through September 2017 in the Combustion Integrated Rack. It studied n-dodecane, n-dodecane/iso-dodecane mixtures (60/40 and 75/25 by mass), and farnesane droplets at pressures from 0.5 to 5 atm and oxygen levels from 17 to 21 percent. Tests included helium dilution of 29 and 59 percent. Sensors measured droplet size, flame size, OH* emission, and radiant output.
profile.experiment_goal: The study set out to learn how cool flame combustion behaves for pure fuels and fuel mixtures over a range of pressures and helium dilution.

results.result_simple: Cool flames can burn steadily around droplets at low temperatures and then go out as the droplet shrinks.
results.result_expert: Cool flames occur in the negative temperature coefficient region at 700 to 900 K. Extinction happens when the droplet gets small enough that heat loss exceeds heat release from low-temperature chemistry.
results.safety_meaning: Cool flames can persist unseen and leave partially burned fuel vapor, which may reignite later.

results.result_simple: Adding helium made cool flames go out sooner, leaving a larger droplet behind.
results.result_expert: Increased helium dilution leads to earlier cool flame extinction and a larger extinction diameter.
results.safety_meaning: Diluent gases change extinction behavior and must be considered in fire safety models.

results.result_simple: Above 2 atm, flames repeatedly switched between hot and cool modes until the fuel was gone.
results.result_expert: At pressures above approximately 2 atm, multiple reignition cycles occurred, alternating hot flame extinction, cool flame, and reignition until complete fuel consumption.
results.safety_meaning: Fires at higher pressure may reignite after appearing to go out.

results.result_simple: Soot shells around droplets became unstable and unclear at higher pressures.
results.result_expert: At higher pressures, the soot shell surrounding the droplet became diffuse and ill-defined, and the mechanism is not fully understood.
results.safety_meaning: Soot behavior at pressure affects smoke detection and fire monitoring.

equipment.note: Cool flame and soot behavior inform smoke and flame detection design.
Reignition and helium dilution results inform extinguisher effectiveness.
Fuel chemistry results help select safer spacecraft materials.

earth_uses: validating chemical kinetic mechanisms for HCCI and RCCI engines
fuel reformulation technologies to produce hydrogen for fuel cell applications

glossary.definition: A low-temperature flame controlled by low-temperature chemistry in the NTC region, around 700 to 900 K.
Negative temperature coefficient region where reaction rate decreases as temperature increases.
Hydroxyl radical emission used to image flame size.
The droplet size at which a cool flame becomes unstable and goes out.

open_questions: The mechanism behind soot-shell instability at higher pressures is not fully understood.
Residual soot surrounding the droplet after hot flame extinction at higher pressures is not fully understood.
All CFI data has yet to be fully analyzed and interpreted using theoretical and numerical models.
